headline_marked: Govt to [[ensure Shakib Al Hasan's security]] if he returns to face cases
headline: Govt to ensure Shakib Al Hasan's security if he returns to face cases
summary: Information Advisor Dr. Zahed Ur Rahman says the cricketer will be safe returning to Bangladesh, but calls him a 'rotten person' for his political ties.
details: Prime Minister's Information Advisor Dr. Zahed Ur Rahman stated that cricketer Shakib Al Hasan will receive full security if he returns to Bangladesh to face legal proceedings.
The statement comes after Shakib told Reuters that he would return to face the cases against him provided he was guaranteed safety from mob violence or attacks.
While guaranteeing security, Dr. Zahed harshly criticized Shakib's personal character, calling him a 'rotten and decayed person' due to his association with former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
The Advisor described Shakib's recent interviews and statements as 'propaganda' and an attempt to create pressure on the government.
Dr. Zahed also mentioned that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has expressed a desire to return to the country in December, and she too would receive constitutional rights and security.
He emphasized that while no 'fascist mafia regime' will be allowed to return, the state will ensure the constitutional and judicial rights of even the most heinous criminals as a democratic nation.
caption:
Will Shakib Al Hasan return to Bangladesh? The government guarantees his security, but the Information Advisor calls him a 'rotten person'.

Prime Minister's Information Advisor Dr. Zahed Ur Rahman stated that cricketer Shakib Al Hasan will receive full security if he returns to Bangladesh to face legal proceedings.

The statement comes after Shakib told Reuters that he would return to face the cases against him provided he was guaranteed safety from mob violence or attacks.

While guaranteeing security, Dr. Zahed harshly criticized Shakib's personal character, calling him a 'rotten and decayed person' due to his association with former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

The Advisor described Shakib's recent interviews and statements as 'propaganda' and an attempt to create pressure on the government.

Dr. Zahed also mentioned that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has expressed a desire to return to the country in December, and she too would receive constitutional rights and security.

He emphasized that while no 'fascist mafia regime' will be allowed to return, the state will ensure the constitutional and judicial rights of even the most heinous criminals as a democratic nation.

headline_marked: Syria court [[sentences ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad to death]] in absentia
headline: Syria court sentences ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia
summary: The former leader was convicted of crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the country's 14-year civil war.
details: A Syrian court in Damascus has sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia. He was convicted of atrocities committed during the country's nearly 14-year civil war.

The court found Assad guilty of premeditated murder, the intentional killing of children under 15, torture, and deprivation of liberty, classifying these acts as crimes against humanity and war crimes.
This is the first major ruling under Syria's transitional leaders, who ousted Assad in December 2024 after a lightning offensive by Islamist-led forces.
Six other former military and security officials, including Assad's brother Maher, were also sentenced to death in absentia for similar crimes.
Former security official Atif Najib, the only defendant present in court, was also sentenced to death for crimes against humanity committed while he was head of political security in Daraa province.
The Syrian civil war, which began in 2011 after the torture of students in Daraa, resulted in over 500,000 deaths and the displacement of millions of people.
Assad, who took power in 2000, fled to Moscow following the collapse of his regime in late 2024.
